title: No second run: loop design, effort dials and AI as SME infrastructure
summary: Anthropic says to drop "think hard" and start Opus 5.5 at Medium, two huge permissively licensed open-weights agent models land, and new NBER papers show embedded AI lifting small sellers' sales by 51.6% and an LLM interviewer beating O*NET on task coverage. The deep dive looks at how a team ran self-improvement loops around a pre-training run it could only do once, and what that teaches about agent loops, verifiers and proxies that lie.
shownotes:
Effort is the new prompt: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 guide says delete "think hard" and start at Medium; Fable 5.2 shows per-token price no longer predicts per-task cost.
Open-weights agent models: Meituan's LongCat-2.5 (1.6T total / 48B active, MIT, W4A4) and Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small (594B / 17B active, Apache 2.0, variable effort).
NBER w36003: generative AI embedded in a Chinese e-commerce platform raised small sellers' monthly sales by 51.6%.
NBER w35987: TaskNet, an LLM interviewer that builds occupational task lists with better coverage than O*NET.
Deep dive: "No Second Run" (GAIR-NLP) on decomposing an unrepeatable pre-training run into verifiable inner loops, context logs of negative results, and proxies that falsely stagnate.
